skill.name: conductor-manage
skill.description: Manage Conductor track lifecycle tasks, including list, archive, restore, rename, delete, and cleanup workflows.
skill.summary: Organizes Conductor track files and metadata across active, archived, and cleanup states.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline path formatting, and ordinary error text. Semantic review found one real risk in the delete workflow because a track-id placeholder is used directly in destructive remove commands without explicit path normalization. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Destructive delete workflow accepts a track-id placeholder before building filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate track IDs before any path use, rejecting slashes, dot segments, absolute paths, and IDs outside the expected pattern.

remediation.issue: Permanent deletion uses recursive remove commands on interpolated track paths.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the canonical path under conductor/tracks and prefer moving data to a quarantine folder before irreversible deletion.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Destructive Track Deletion
semantic_findings.description: The delete flow accepts a track-id argument and later uses that placeholder in recursive remove commands. Without explicit path normalization and ID validation, a malformed ID could delete files outside the intended Conductor track directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The playbook clearly combines user-supplied track IDs with rm -rf paths. Existing confirmation steps reduce accidental deletion, but they do not prove path confinement.

content.value_statement: Conductor repositories can accumulate stale tracks, archived work, and inconsistent metadata. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through track lifecycle operations.
actual_capabilities: Detects operation mode from arguments or presents an interactive management menu.
Lists active, completed, and archived Conductor tracks with status context.
Archives completed tracks and restores archived tracks with confirmation prompts.
Renames track IDs and updates registry and metadata references.
Finds orphaned directories, registry entries, incomplete tracks, and stale work.
Documents delete workflows with warnings, confirmations, and git commit steps.
limitations: Requires an initialized Conductor repository with the expected directory structure.
Does not recover deleted track files unless a separate backup or git history exists.
Does not rename historical git commits or old references outside tracked metadata.
Needs careful human review for delete and cleanup actions.

use_cases.title: Archive Completed Delivery Work
use_cases.description: Move finished Conductor tracks into the archive while keeping registry metadata consistent.

use_cases.title: Restore Prior Planning Context
use_cases.description: Bring an archived track back into active work when a feature or fix resumes.

use_cases.title: Clean Project Tracking Drift
use_cases.description: Review orphaned folders, missing metadata, and stale in-progress tracks before release planning.

prompt_templates.title: List Track Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-manage to list all Conductor tracks and summarize active, completed, and archived work.

prompt_templates.title: Archive Completed Tracks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-manage to find completed tracks that can be archived. Ask for confirmation before changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Restore Or Rename A Track
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-manage to restore an archived track or rename a track ID. Validate conflicts before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit And Cleanup Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-manage cleanup mode to identify orphaned artifacts, incomplete tracks, and stale work. Propose fixes before editing.

output_examples.input: List every Conductor track before a planning meeting.
output: A grouped overview of active, completed, and archived tracks.
Progress counts, recent update dates, and archive readiness notes.

output_examples.input: Archive completed tracks after a release.
output: A confirmation screen listing the tracks selected for archive.
A completion summary showing moved tracks, updated metadata, and the recorded commit.
A categorized issue list for orphaned directories, missing registry entries, incomplete tracks, and stale work.
Recommended fixes that wait for approval before modifying repository files.

best_practices: Run list mode first so track state is clear before making changes.
Back up important track data before delete or cleanup operations.
Review generated changes in tracks.md and metadata before committing.
anti_patterns: Do not use delete mode when archive mode would preserve useful context.
Do not run cleanup fixes without reading the issue list first.
Do not rename tracks without checking for references in related documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It manages Conductor tracks, including listing, archive, restore, rename, delete, and cleanup workflows.

faq.question: Can it work outside a Conductor repository?
faq.answer: No. It expects conductor/product.md, conductor/tracks.md, and conductor/tracks/ to exist.

faq.question: Does delete mode require confirmation?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook requires explicit confirmation and warns when a track is in progress.

faq.question: Can archived tracks be restored?
faq.answer: Yes. The restore flow checks for conflicts, moves the track back, and updates registry metadata.

faq.question: Does rename mode update git history?
faq.answer: No. It updates current track files and metadata, but historical commits keep their original references.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
